Day 2. [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] packed for the hill: six stones out of the jar of forty-three, including the grey one with the white stripe, Captain Crunch wrapped in a handkerchief in the middle of the canvas bag, and the leather notebook. He could not have said what the stones were for. He brought the fossil because it had been somewhere, and because if anything was going to be lucky it would be that.

Bruno was waiting at the kitchen door with the leash already in his mouth, which nobody had asked him to fetch. He did not whine and did not press against [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO]'s leg — he simply stood and waited. His mother, who knew exactly what was happening and made no fuss about it, said the rule back to him at the door and corrected him on it: not when the sun is starting to touch the horizon, when it touches.

At the fountain in the afternoon Rosa found him. She had asked her father five times what is on the other side of the hill and got "less interesting than you think" every time, which she does not believe. [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] has not asked Marcos yet, though he thinks Marcos would answer — in a story, circling, the way he does. Rosa argued her way in and ended it with "Then I'm coming too."

Who knows what: Rosa knows he is going up the hill. Nobody in the village will say what is beyond it, and nobody seems to think it is their business. Still open: what is over the hill; what Marcos knows; what [NOMBRE_ANONIMIZADO] is really afraid of.
